sentences.span: expecting nonfarm payrolls to rebound by +65k
sentences.why: Every 2026-09-04 source is a pre-release morning note; NFP is a forecast (DB +65k, JPM Feroli 50k vs Street 55k) in every document. Nothing in the corpus is an actual print, so 'the official number says the opposite' asserts a released outcome the sources never confirm — forecast presented as a print.

sentences.span: slash the chance of a hike to 51% as of this morning, down from 63%
sentences.why: The 60-70% pricing window since Aug 31 and Waller's Thursday dovish break are supported. But 'this morning put it back' implies odds rebounded upward; both DB (51% this morning) and JPM (~50% vs 65% Monday) show odds holding near 50%, not reversing back toward 60-70%.

sentences.span: showed a 58%m/m increase in job cuts, but the longer-run trend looks good
sentences.why: CPI-over-NFP framing and the 58% MoM figure are correctly attributed to JPMorgan. But JPM's own note explicitly says the 58% jump does NOT signal underlying weakness ('longer-run trend looks good'); using it as evidence the labor detail is 'softer than headline' inverts JPM's stated conclusion.

sentences.span: The three-month average is down 33%oya, the August total was the lowest August reading since 2022
sentences.why: Both figures match verbatim, correctly attributed to JPMorgan, and the conclusion (layoff data doesn't carry the dovish case) matches JPM's own framing that layoffs remain low.

sentences.span: Silicon Data's LLM Token Expenditure Index...fell 29% in August and printed about $0.97 per million tokens at month-end
sentences.why: All figures are accurate but the single trailing '(JPMorgan)' attribution misattributes the whole sentence. The headline Silicon Data index figures (-29%, $0.97, ~half May peak) are Goldman's; only the OpenRouter volume/spend figures are JPMorgan's (cited secondhand inside the Goldman note).

sentences.span: Compute scarcity has been driving hyperscaler outperformance recently.
sentences.why: Bank attribution (TS Lombard) and the compute-scarcity-drives-outperformance claim are verbatim-matched; 'usage pays for itself' is a fair paraphrase of the falling-token-price/rising-volume mechanism the note describes.

sentences.span: Broadcom expects its AI semiconductor revenue to double in FY27 to $115bn... raise our 12-month target price to $540
sentences.why: The $540 target, $115bn FY27 figure, and Buy rating are accurate, and they do sit in tension with a bearish pricing view from the same bank — but that bank is Goldman Sachs, not TS Lombard, which is the house s6 named as 'the other side'. 'The same house' misattributes the AVGO call.

sentences.span: high-frequency visible oil data likely underestimate recent inventories
sentences.why: Goldman's dark-tanker-crossing analysis directly supports that visible supply data understates the true picture; attribution and direction match.

sentences.span: we estimate recent total Persian Gulf oil exports at roughly 15-16mb/d or 2/3 of pre-war levels, while... visible exports stand at only 10mb/d
sentences.why: Every figure matches exactly (15-16mb/d total, 10mb/d visible, two-thirds of pre-war, Oman-area AIS-off tanker crossings), correctly attributed to Goldman.

Searched all 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-04 source-text and source-text-all files for 'mispric*' and 'layer' in any relevant sense (oil, vol/positioning files including McElligott, GS vol traders, global-equity-volatility-insights); no document uses this framing. No source supports the claim.

sentences.span: midterm elections have rarely elicited large broad market moves historically
sentences.why: Directly matches BofA's stated rationale for the muted priced move; correct attribution and direction.

sentences.span: options on regional banks (KRE) and small caps (RTY) appear most underpriced today relative to their 2024 election-week moves... we like structures like IWM puts
sentences.why: Both the underpriced-vs-2024 claim and the near-record-steep tail skew rationale for choosing IWM puts over index protection are explicitly stated in the same BofA note, correctly attributed.

sentences.span: S&P vol is pricing in a relatively muted 0.82% move following this year's elections
sentences.why: 0.82% is explicitly the S&P/broad-index implied move, not an IWM/small-cap figure, and the note never claims the IWM puts expire worthless if that prints — its whole thesis is that small-cap/regional-bank vol is underpriced relative to 2024, i.e. the IWM puts could still pay off even with a muted index move. The sentence misapplies a real source figure to draw an unsupported, thesis-contradicting conclusion.

sentences.span: hence, SPX Skew and Put Skew back to 2%ile
sentences.why: The 0.2 percentile (IWM) and 5th percentile (dispersion) figures are McElligott's own statements, but the middle '2nd percentile' SPX-protection figure is explicitly attributed in the source to Goldman's Brian Garrett, not McElligott. Bundling all three under a single '(Nomura's McElligott)' tag misattributes one of the three statistics.

sentences.span: options market makers and dealers are choking on huge PNL losses, as anybody or anything long Optionality / long Skew has been bled-out
sentences.why: The 'market makers taking real losses' line is explicitly tied in the source to the IVol/skew collapse item, not to the dispersion-percentile item ('that last one' in s14's list). The dispersion bullet independently implies losses but the pairing plus the added phrase 'not a market at peace' (not in source) stretches the attribution beyond what the text supports for that specific item.
